(Tonight through next Wednesday) 

WEATHER PATTERN OVERVIEW: Active weather pattern will continue as 
the next strong upper level trough is currently impacting the 
Silver State and will continue to do so through Friday evening. 
This system is on track to bring several rounds of rain and snow 
to the Great Basin region. Snow levels have fallen below 6000 feet
early Thursday AM, but will vary Thursday before dropping to 
valley floors by late Thursday evening to early Friday morning. 
Transition to all snow could happen sooner if temperatures run 
cooler than forecast due to wet-bulb effects. Overall accumulating
snows will be likely for most with the lower elevation valleys 
seeing between 0.5” and 3”, higher elevation valleys could see 
between 2” to 5” of new snow. For passes and road summits rain 
will change over to snow quicker leading to between 4” to 7” of 
snowfall, with the mountain ranges seeing all snow with this event
with totals between 8” to 18” plus possible. 

Another factor to take into account with this system will be 
winds, as gusty S to SW winds will be possible through Friday. 
Especially for central Nevada as N Nye, White Pine, southern 
Lander, and southern Eureka Counties could see South to Southwest
winds of 20 to 30 MPH with gusts up to 40 MPH possible. Further 
north, winds aren’t expected to be as strong, but will still be 
breezy at 15 to 25 MPH with gust up to 35 MPH possible. The 
combination of winds and snowfall will bring adverse to hazardous 
driving conditions for area highways Thursday evening through 
Friday. For this reason a Winter Storm Warning has been issued 
for the Ruby Mountains, and a winter Weather Advisory for parts 
of Elko, Eureka, Lander, Humboldt, and White Pine Counties through
Friday evening. Friday a cold front will push through the region 
which will shift wind to the NW with breezy conditions continuing 
with speeds of 10 to 20 MPH with gusts up the 30 MPH possible. 
Also for Friday the main upper trough will pass overhead, and with
that will be the possibility for convective snow showers and snow
squalls. These event could bring a boost to local snow totals. 
Central Nevada will see the greatest chances for these features as
instability, what little there is will be concentrated along the 
US 50 corridor. Temperatures for this event will likely depend on 
precipitation mechanics as areas with active precipitation will be
cooler due to wet bulb effects, only to rebound as breaks in 
precipitation occur. Overall highs will range in the low 30s to 
low 40s with lows in the upper 20s through Saturday morning. 

With the exit of this upper trough, Saturday will see a brief 
break as a short wave ridge passes through. This break, however, 
will be short lived as another upper level trough will start to 
move through Sunday afternoon through Monday evening. This system 
looks to be weaker and faster than Thursdays storm, but could have
the potential to bring isolated rain/snow showers with 
accumulations of 0.5” to 2” of snow for the passes and range 
summits, and up to 0.10” of rain for the valleys. Tuesday will 
bring another quick break in the action before another system will
try to move through for next Wednesday with more chances for 
rain/snow showers. Temperature for the rest of the week look to 
remain near to or below normal as highs look to range in the upper
30s to upper 40s with lows in the upper teens to 20s for 
overnight lows.


FORECAST CONFIDENCE & DEVIATIONS: There is high confidence in winter 
precipitation and breezy winds Thursday and Friday with 
accumulation snows possible to likely for parts of NE Nevada.

High confidence remains in the coldest temperatures so far
Saturday night behind the system currently impacting the region.

There is medium confidence for another, weaker upper level trough
passage across Nevada Sunday and Monday. 
     
There is low to medium confidence of the continuation of the 
active upper pattern as a third upper trough pushing into the 
western US for next Wednesday.
